subject: EverPay: clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@everpay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: ops-security@everpay.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the SOC-2 package earlier. Our security team is working through the BCP/DR section and has a couple of clarifying asks before we mark the control satisfied:

1) For each outlined failover scenario in your runbook, can you confirm the demonstrated RTO and RPO from the most recent full-scale test?
2) We need the specific dates, scope, and short test logs (or summary) showing the actual recovery steps and timings — redacted is fine.
3) Are there any known single points of failure in the public-hosted (shared) environment that would push the RTO beyond the stated SLA?

We are on a tight timeline for our compliance gate — could you provide this by end of week? Happy to jump on a 20-min call if needed.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Shah
Senior Security Manager, EverPay
ops-security@everpay.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@everpay.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list. I can get you the test artifacts and a short mapping from scenario -> observed RTO/RPO.

Quick bullets on scope:
- We run full regional failover drills quarterly and partial component failovers monthly.
- Most recent full regional drill: 2026-03-30 (we have logs and timing snapshots).
- Shared-hosted (multi-tenant) paths have documented fallback to Dedicated backfill; worst-case documented RTO under that path is listed in the snapshot.

I am attaching the runbook excerpt and the RTO/RPO snapshot to this message; Marcus can add the log snippets and technical notes on single points of failure.

Attachments: DR_runbook_v3.pdf; RTO_RPO_snapshot_Q1-2026.xlsx

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety (Compliance)
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@everpay.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Priya — adding a few technical details and the test log excerpt you asked for. High level:

- Full regional failover (primary -> secondary region) on 2026-03-30: observed RTO = 7m45s for control-plane reconvergence; RPO = 0s for persistent stores with cross-region replication; client KV cache warmup to steady-state token latency ~12m.
- Partial service degradation (worker pool saturations): handled by live autoscaling + prefix-KV cache warming; observed RTO = 3m20s.
- Dedicated backfill path (when bursting from hosted to Dedicated): documented failover orchestration introduces an additional 20–35 minutes to reach full capacity for long-running jobs; we treat this as a planned capacity fallback, not a silent POA.

Im attaching the extracted lines from the test log (redacted) and a short timeline table. If you need the full log file we can share via a signed SFTP link or a redacted Drive file.

Attachments: failover_test_log_2026-03-30.txt

Technical note on single points of failure:
- Control plane: replicated across AZs and regions; we have documented manual failover steps if automated path fails, which we exercised in the last drill.
- External vendor for metrics ingestion has a short maintenance window risk; we have an automated circuit-breaker to degrade metrics-only features without impacting core inference path.

Happy to hop on the call to run through specifics.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@everpay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence

Thanks Marcus — that level of detail is helpful. Two quick follow-ups:

1) Can you confirm whether the 0s RPO for persistent stores includes the analytics pipeline (its okay if analytics can lag)?
2) For the dedicated backfill path, do you have a recorded play-by-play checklist that shows the manual/operator steps and the estimated times for each step? Our procurement team wants that as part of their risk assessment.

If you can drop both items into a single zip or a shared Drive folder, that would work.

Thanks,
Priya

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@everpay.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 Apr 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence

Hi Priya — quick answers and link:

1) RPO clarification: the 0s RPO applies to the customer-facing persistent stores (model weights, user prompt state, and primary billing ledger). The analytics pipeline is handled via an eventually consistent stream (it can lag up to 15 minutes during a regional failover). We will mark this explicitly in the snapshot file.

2) Dedicated backfill operator checklist: Ive uploaded a stepwise playbook (operator_checklist_backfill.md) and an estimated timings table to a secured Drive folder here: https://drive.redwood.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-DR-Runbooks. The folder contains the backfill checklist, the runbook PDF we sent earlier, and a redacted copy of the 2026-03-30 test logs.

I will bundle these into a single zip for you and put it in the same folder today. Let me know if EverPay needs the artifacts via SFTP.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Program Manager, Resilience Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@everpay.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2026 15:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarifying DR scenarios and RTO/RPO evidence

Appreciate the fast turnaround — the Drive folder looks good and the checklist answers our procurement questions. Two last asks before we close:

- Can you add a one-paragraph attestation (signed by your Head of Compliance) confirming the dates of the most recent full-scale drills and that the attached logs are unmodified extracts?
- We also need a short note on the retention policy for test artifacts (how long you keep logs/test snapshots) so our audit team can verify archival controls.

If you can drop both items into the Drive folder by EOD Wednesday our SOC reviewer will mark the BCP control as satisfied.

Thanks again — Priya
